comment: Cross-implementation anchor for the run-plan contract (kernel/src/run-plan.ts): what a plan is, and how to digest one so two shells and a ledger can say 'this run was held to this plan'. Rules a second implementation must reproduce, stated here so it need not read the TypeScript: (1) schemaVersion is exactly `iterate.run-plan/0.1`. (2) `dimensions` is 1..64 entries, each an object with a required `id` matching `^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$` and at most 64 chars, and optional `label` (<=256) and `focus` (<=4096); no other keys. An empty plan is refused: a run with nothing to verify has a configuration problem, and reporting 0/0 dimensions as success is how that gets hidden. (3) Planned order is the caller's and is never sorted. (4) A repeated id is refused, not collapsed — the two entries can carry different focus, so collapsing picks one silently. JSON Schema cannot express id-level uniqueness (`uniqueItems` compares whole objects), so that rule lives on the validator side; the case named `duplicate-ids-differ-only-by-focus` below is the documented shape where the published schema accepts and the validator refuses. (5) `source`, when present, has a required `kind` in `config|recipe|session|manual` and an optional non-empty `name` <=512; nothing here reads a config file to invent a source. (6) The digest is `rp_` + sha256 of the canonical JSON form: UTF-16-code-unit-sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, arrays in order, strings as JSON escapes them; numbers use the host's shortest roundtrip form, which is why none appear in this fixture — that concern is pinned by the canonical-JSON cases in the C35 suite instead. Provenance: the nine ids and both focus strings are taken verbatim from GlassPane's own iterate.config.yaml (`dimensions:` and `dimension_sets.engine|gui.focus`), because a vocabulary invented for a fixture would let both sides agree on something neither product uses. The one `label` value is NOT from that config — it has no label vocabulary at all — and is written here to pin that a label is accepted, is optional, and is part of the digest; treat that string as fixture vocabulary, not as a name either product displays.
